dehydrated_text:
What do you do in this situation? You cut the rope; okay, you die. Your life isn't what matters; your family and team do. In war, especially trench warfare, soldiers often jump on grenades to save comrades with no time to pick up or throw them away.

You just do it because saving your comrades is paramount. This leads to a synchronicity where you read each other's minds, and this continues for 10-20 years. Suddenly, you're transported back to the real world but retain memories of hell on Monkey Island. You've worked together, developed a hive mind, and are inspired.

You're driven by a new religion. Upon returning, many want to reassemble, sharing experiences with children and grandchildren who will inherit your legacy and become secret elites controlling power in the world.

If you were just a peasant before, real power still lies with you guys. You develop strange rituals like funeral rites involving eating the sacrifice, maintaining unity despite external leadership.

This is similar to Sparta's historical example, where 300 Spartan soldiers fought to the death against overwhelming Persian forces at Thermopylae, inspiring Greeks by their sacrifice.
